```{r}
data(AirPassengers)
AP <- AirPassengers
AP
class(AP)
start(AP)
end(AP)
frequency(AP)
plot(
  AP,
  ylab = "Number of Passengers",
  xlab = "Year",
  main = "Monthly Airline Passenger Numbers 1949-1960"
)
```

- trend: a systematic change that does not appear to be periodic
- seasonal variation: applied generally to repeating patterns within any fixed period of time (e.g. days of the week)
- cycles: pattern that do not correspond to some fix ed period of time (e.g. business cycles)

In the absence of some shock to the system, trends generally change slowly, therefore linear extrapolation is good approzimation for the few steps ahead. 
- Higher-order polynomials can be used for historic fits
- Linear extrapolation for short-term forecasts
- Forecasts longer then a year are better called scenarios, expecting trends to continue lineraly for many years is often unrealistic.

Data cleaning
- Erroneous values such as missing data (often coded a negative value)
- Outliers - investigate.  If correct, they should not be excluded but consider more robust methods.

Coding
- use `aggregate` to aggregate to annual-level and remove seasonal component.  
- Use a boxplot to visualize a summary of values for each season, use the `cycle` function to extract seasons for each item of data.
- Use `layout` to arrange multiple plots on a single page.

```{r}
layout(1:2)
plot(aggregate(AP))
boxplot(AP~cycle(AP))
```

Monthly Employment Rates for Maine: 
```{r}
www <- "C:\\Users\\BASHCROF\\git-repos\\github\\Introductory-Time-Series-with-R-Datasets\\data\\Maine.dat"
Maine.month <- read.table(www, header = TRUE)
attach(Maine.month)

# reads in as a dataframe, with column unemploy
class(Maine.month) 
head(Maine.month)

# turn column unemploy into a ts object
# use start and end to subset of the data
Maine.month.ts <- ts(unemploy, start = c(1986,1), end = c(1990,12), freq = 12)
class(Maine.month.ts)
```

```{r}
# use the entire data
Maine.month.ts <- ts(unemploy, start = c(1986,1), freq = 12)

# get mean annual rate
Maine.annual.ts <- aggregate(Maine.month.ts, nfrequency = 1)

# plot both time series
layout(1:2)
plot(Maine.month.ts, main = "Monthly Employment Rates for Maine", ylab = "Unemployed (%)")
plot(Maine.annual.ts, main = "Annual Employment Rates for Maine", ylab = "Unemployed (%)")

# Calculate the precise percentages using window
# sample with a frequency of "frequency"
Maine.Feb <- window(Maine.month.ts, start = c(1996,2), freq=TRUE)
Maine.Aug <- window(Maine.month.ts, start = c(1996,8), freq=TRUE)
Feb.ratio = mean(Maine.Feb)/mean(Maine.month.ts)
Aug.ratio = mean(Maine.Aug)/mean(Maine.month.ts)
Feb.ratio
Aug.ratio
```
